players.product: memory package substrates (FBGA / FC-FBGA for PC, server and mobile DRAM incl. DDR5) and leadframes

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 (DART half-year report, consolidated, reviewed by Daejoo Accounting): revenue KRW 399,737,755,086 against KRW 294,860,888,771 in H1 2025 and operating profit KRW 35,844,976,077 against KRW 8,582,729,707; Q2 alone revenue KRW 211,085,611,184 (Q2 2025: KRW 157,382,615,237) with operating profit KRW 24,866,714,290 (KRW 8,228,054,891). Mix: leadframes KRW 304,532M (76.18%) and package substrates KRW 95,204M (23.82%); exports were 97.6% of revenue. Average package-substrate export price was KRW 73,406/Kpcs (US$49.48) against KRW 73,626/Kpcs (US$51.77) in FY2025, domestic KRW 80,260/Kpcs against KRW 76,414. Raw-material unit costs rose sharply year on year (copper +30.8%, gold +42.0%, silver +109.5%, palladium +42.6%); the company links product prices to metal prices by agreement with customers.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 rev KRW 399,737,755,086 (vs KRW 294,860,888,771); H1 OP KRW 35,844,976,077 (vs KRW 8,582,729,707); Q2 rev KRW 211,085,611,184, Q2 OP KRW 24,866,714,290; leadframe 76.18% / package substrate 23.82%; substrate export ASP KRW 73,406/Kpcs (US$49.48)

quarterly_data.signal: Customers (DART half-year report): package-substrate customers are mainly Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, served at their Korean and Chinese plants; leadframe customers are IDMs Infineon, ST Micro and NXP and OSATs ASE, Amkor, SPIL, JCET and UTAC. The company withholds each customer's revenue share. Two unnamed customers each exceeded 10% of consolidated revenue in H1 2026: KRW 49,476,635 thousand (12.38%) and KRW 44,810,728 thousand (11.21%), against 13.11% and 13.02% a year earlier. Orders are placed for delivery within 1~2 months with volumes and prices set monthly or quarterly, so no backlog is disclosed and there is no long-term supply contract.
quarterly_data.figure: Two customers at 12.38% (KRW 49,476,635 thousand) and 11.21% (KRW 44,810,728 thousand) of H1 revenue (H1 2025: 13.11% / 13.02%)
quarterly_data.counterparty: Samsung, SK Hynix (package substrates); Infineon, STMicroelectronics, NXP, ASE, Amkor, SPIL, JCET, UTAC (leadframes)

quarterly_data.signal: Raw-material suppliers (DART half-year report): H1 2026 purchases were copper KRW 70,310M (27.8%, from Poongsan and others), gold KRW 89,846M (35.5%, from Torykom and others), CCL laminate KRW 28,532M (11.3%, from Panasonic and others), silver KRW 41,789M (16.5%) and palladium KRW 20,492M (8.1%, both from Yuchang Metal and others), KRW 252,957M in total; the company says supplier concentration is low and it is diversifying sources.
quarterly_data.figure: Materials purchases KRW 252,957M: gold KRW 89,846M, copper KRW 70,310M, silver KRW 41,789M, CCL KRW 28,532M, palladium KRW 20,492M
quarterly_data.counterparty: Poongsan (copper), Torykom (gold), Panasonic (CCL), Yuchang Metal (silver, palladium)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and investment (DART half-year report): with 557 production tools, H1 2026 output was 26,328,492 Kpcs against capacity of 47,600,043 Kpcs, utilisation 55.3% (FY2025: 48.9%; strip basis 51.4% against 46.3%). H1 investment of KRW 8,393M went to a new manufacturing building, etching equipment and CO2 laser drills to meet rising customer demand, and the company says this is extending its substrate business from existing memory packages into mobile DRAM, graphics DRAM and NAND flash packages. The board approved a BGA (package-substrate) capacity expansion investment on 2026-05-29 and an AI-based BGA final-inspection investment; the Changwon facility expansion program, revised to KRW 252,500,000,000, runs to 2026-11-30, and after the period the company appointed a panel-line build TF leader.
quarterly_data.figure: Utilisation 55.3% (26,328,492 of 47,600,043 Kpcs; FY2025 48.9%); H1 capex KRW 8,393M; BGA capacity expansion approved 2026-05-29; facility program KRW 252,500,000,000 to 2026-11-30
